knowledge:
- key_parameters: model_name=The name of the machine learning model to use (e.g., "Prosit_2019_intensity", "ms2pip_HCD2021") ;; server_url=The URL of the Koina server instance (e.g., "koina.wilhelmlab.org") ;; peptide_sequences=Character vector of peptide sequences in the input data frame ;; collision_energies=Numeric vector of collision energies in the input data frame ;; precursor_charges=Integer vector of precursor charges in the input data frame
- alternatives: predictWithKoinaModel=An alternative functional (pass-by-value) interface to the R6 class method prosit2019$predict() ;; OrgMassSpecR::SpectrumSimilarity=Used to compare and calculate similarity scores between predicted spectra from different models
- when_to_use: When predicting peptide fragment intensities, retention times, or other properties using deep learning models (like Prosit or MS2PIP) without hosting the models locally or having specialized GPU hardware.
- pitfalls: Input data frame column names must match exactly what the model expects (e.g., peptide_sequences, collision_energies, precursor_charges) ;; Output structure and columns vary depending on the chosen model ;; Internet connectivity is required to communicate with the remote Koina server, though packages like httptest can be used to cache responses for testing.

workflows.name: peptide_fragment_intensity_prediction
workflows.intent: Predict peptide fragment ion intensities and m/z values using a remote Koina model.
input: peptide_data.csv (Data frame containing peptide sequences, collision energies, and precursor charges)
workflows.stages: 1. Initialize the Koina client with a specific model and server using koinar::Koina() ;; 2. Prepare the input data frame with peptide sequences, collision energies, and precursor charges ;; 3. Fetch predictions using the $predict() method or koinar::predictWithKoinaModel()
workflows.code:
prosit2019 <- koinar::Koina(
  model_name = "Prosit_2019_intensity",
  server_url = "koina.wilhelmlab.org"
)
input <- data.frame(
  peptide_sequences = c("LGGNEQVTR", "GAGSSEPVTGLDAK"),
  collision_energies = c(25, 25),
  precursor_charges = c(1, 2)
)
prediction_results <- prosit2019$predict(input)
prediction_results <- koinar::predictWithKoinaModel(prosit2019, input)

workflows.name: spectral_similarity_comparison
workflows.intent: Compare peptide fragment ion intensity predictions between two different models (e.g., Prosit and MS2PIP).
input: peptide_data.csv (Data frame containing peptide sequences, collision energies, and precursor charges)
workflows.stages: 1. Initialize Koina clients for both models using koinar::Koina() ;; 2. Predict fragment intensities for both models using $predict() ;; 3. Compare the predicted spectra using OrgMassSpecR::SpectrumSimilarity()
workflows.code:
input <- data.frame(
  peptide_sequences = c(
    "LGGNEQVTR", "YILAGVENSK", "GTFIIDPGGVIR", "GTFIIDPAAVIR",
    "GAGSSEPVTGLDAK", "TPVISGGPYEYR", "VEATFGVDESNAK",
    "TPVITGAPYEYR", "DGLDAASYYAPVR", "ADVTPADFSEWSK",
    "LFLQFGAQGSPFLK"
  ),
  collision_energies = 35,
  precursor_charges = 2
)
prosit2019 <- koinar::Koina(
  model_name = "Prosit_2019_intensity",
  server_url = "koina.wilhelmlab.org"
)
pred_prosit <- prosit2019$predict((input))
pred_prosit$model <- "Prosit_2019_intensity"

ms2pip <- koinar::Koina(
  model_name = "ms2pip_HCD2021",
  server_url = "koina.wilhelmlab.org"
)

pred_ms2pip <- ms2pip$predict(input)
pred_ms2pip$model <- "ms2pip_HCD2021"

peptide_sequence <- "ADVTPADFSEWSK"

sim <- OrgMassSpecR::SpectrumSimilarity(pred_prosit[pred_prosit$peptide_sequences == peptide_sequence, c("mz", "intensities")],
  pred_ms2pip[pred_ms2pip$peptide_sequences == peptide_sequence, c("mz", "intensities")],
  top.lab = "Prosit",
  bottom.lab = "MS2PIP",
  b = 25
)
title(main = paste(peptide_sequence, "| Spectrum similarity", round(sim, 3)))
